notes: 8 configurations, 7 machines, 5 manufacturers (RICOR, ORTEC/AMETEK, Mirion/Canberra, Tristan Technologies, Tenney/TPS). Categories covered: integral rotary Stirling IR coolers (K508 77 K class, K562S HOT 95-150 K), Stirling/electrically cooled HPGe RIIDs (Detective X, Falcon 5000), HTS 77 K SQUID magnetometer (G377), MIL-STD-810 Method 503 / MIL-STD-883 1010 thermal-shock chambers (Tenney TS2-2, TS2-8), thermal-vacuum chamber (Tenney economical TVAC). Not covered (no reachable spec text this run; WebSearch budget and Tavily quota were exhausted): linear split Stirling/pulse-tube coolers (Thales, AIM, Teledyne FLIR FL-100 brochure has MTTF only), HTS degaussing systems (research demonstrators, not catalog products), stand-alone MIL-STD-810 climatic chambers (already covered by automotive BINDER/ESPEC/Thermotron files). Conventions: for RIIDs temperature.range/base are the instrument operating (ambient/measured-object) range, since the measured source is outside the instrument and the crystal temperature is unpublished; external-measurement instruments (RIIDs, G377) record sample.diameter/height as not_available (no sample space). Bare cryocoolers: temperature.range = cold-tip range, sample.diameter.max = cold-finger OD (8 mm, from the K508 drawing callout 'O.D. Ø8' and K562S text '8mm Cold Finger'), vacuum.available false (dewar supplied by the IDCA integrator). Tenney TS2 numbers come from an image-only spec-table PDF that was rendered and transcribed; the TS2 product load '200*' is footnoted as the carriage limit with recovery to be reviewed by the factory. Falcon 5000 evidence is the 2015 DHS SAVER market survey (reference_data), not a Mirion datasheet (mirion.com returned 403). Tristan G377 datasheet is dated 2007 but the model is still listed on tristantech.com/general. Typical-only values (Ricor/Detective X cool-down) are stored as published since no guaranteed value exists. Cooling power stored in mW (vocabulary canonical nW; exact conversion).
